questions.q: A 35-year-old farmer presents with a painless nodule on the dorsum of his hand that has been enlarging for 3 months. It started as a small papule at the site of a thorn prick and now shows sporotrichoid spread with nodules along the lymphatics of the forearm. The most likely causative organism is:
questions.exp: Sporothrix schenckii causes sporotrichosis, classically presenting as a primary inoculation site with lymphocutaneous spread along lymphatics (sporotrichoid pattern). Thorn prick is a classic history. Treated with itraconazole.

questions.q: A 28-year-old sexually active man presents with painless ulcer on the glans with clean base and indurated edges, associated with bilateral non-tender inguinal lymphadenopathy. Dark-field microscopy reveals spirochetes. The drug of choice for this condition is:
opts: Benzathine penicillin G 2.4 MU IM single dose
questions.exp: Primary syphilis presents with a painless chancre and non-tender lymphadenopathy. Treponema pallidum is the causative organism. Benzathine penicillin G 2.4 MU IM as a single dose is the drug of choice for primary and secondary syphilis.

questions.q: A 45-year-old man from a leprosy-endemic area presents with hypopigmented anaesthetic patches on trunk and extremities. Slit-skin smear shows a Bacterial Index of 4+. Nerve biopsy shows foamy macrophages (Virchow cells) laden with AFB arranged in globi. This patient should be treated with:
questions.exp: BI of 4+ and globi on biopsy indicate multibacillary (MB) leprosy. WHO MDT for MB leprosy is Rifampicin 600 mg monthly + Clofazimine 300 mg monthly + Clofazimine 50 mg daily + Dapsone 100 mg daily for 12 months.

questions.q: A 22-year-old woman develops tense bullae on normal-appearing skin and mucous membranes. Nikolsky sign is negative. DIF shows linear IgG and C3 deposits along the basement membrane zone. The pathognomonic autoantigen is:
questions.exp: Bullous pemphigoid (BP) presents with tense bullae, negative Nikolsky sign, linear IgG and C3 at BMZ on DIF. Autoantigens are BP230 (hemidesmosome plaque protein) and BP180 (type XVII collagen, transmembrane protein).

questions.q: A 55-year-old man on methotrexate for psoriasis develops megaloblastic anaemia and oral ulcers. The mechanism by which methotrexate causes this adverse effect is:
opts: Inhibition of dihydrofolate reductase leading to folate deficiency
questions.exp: Methotrexate inhibits dihydrofolate reductase (DHFR), preventing conversion of dihydrofolate to tetrahydrofolate. This impairs DNA synthesis causing megaloblastic anaemia and mucositis. Folinic acid (leucovorin) supplementation can mitigate this.

questions.q: A 30-year-old woman presents with malar rash, photosensitivity, and oral ulcers. ANA is positive with anti-dsDNA antibodies. She develops nephrotic syndrome. Which complement pathway abnormality is classically associated with this condition?
questions.exp: Systemic lupus erythematosus (SLE) activates both classical and alternative complement pathways. Active lupus nephritis classically causes consumption of both C3 and C4, distinguishing it from other glomerulonephritides. Low C3+C4 correlates with disease activity.

questions.q: A 40-year-old HIV-positive patient (CD4 count 80 cells/µL) presents with painful grouped vesicles on an erythematous base along the T6 dermatome. The antiviral drug of choice and its mechanism of action is:
opts: Famciclovir; inhibits DNA polymerase after phosphorylation by viral thymidine kinase
questions.exp: Herpes zoster is caused by VZV reactivation. Famciclovir (prodrug of penciclovir) or valacyclovir are preferred for herpes zoster as they have better bioavailability than acyclovir. All act by inhibiting viral DNA polymerase after phosphorylation by viral thymidine kinase.

questions.q: A 25-year-old presents with a rapidly growing smooth nodule on the lower lip. Excision shows a well-circumscribed tumour of spindle cells arranged in short fascicles with a 'herringbone' pattern, with cells positive for CD34 on immunohistochemistry. The diagnosis is:
questions.exp: Dermatofibrosarcoma protuberans (DFSP) is a low-grade fibroblastic tumour showing spindle cells in a storiform/herringbone pattern. CD34 positivity is characteristic. It is locally aggressive with low metastatic potential. Associated with t(17;22) translocation.

questions.q: A 60-year-old man with long-standing plaque psoriasis develops joint pain and 'pencil-in-cup' deformity on X-ray. HLA-B27 is negative. The most likely diagnosis is:
questions.exp: Arthritis mutilans is the most severe form of psoriatic arthritis, characterised by osteolysis causing 'pencil-in-cup' deformity and 'opera glass' fingers. It is seronegative (RF negative) and not strongly associated with HLA-B27 (unlike ankylosing spondylitis).

questions.q: During a patch test, a patient shows a 2+ reaction at 48 hours to a standard allergen. At 96-hour reading, the reaction has diminished significantly. This pattern is best described as:
questions.exp: A decrescendo reaction (diminishing reaction) is one that is positive at 48 hours but weaker or negative at 96-hour reading, suggesting an irritant reaction rather than true allergic contact dermatitis. True allergic reactions typically persist or increase from 48 to 96 hours (crescendo).

questions.q: A 20-year-old presents with sudden onset acute urticaria after eating shellfish. Mast cell degranulation in this IgE-mediated reaction releases all of the following preformed mediators EXCEPT:
questions.exp: Mast cell granules contain preformed mediators: histamine, tryptase, chymase, heparin, and carboxypeptidase A. Prostaglandin D2 (PGD2) is a newly synthesised lipid mediator generated from arachidonic acid after mast cell activation — it is NOT preformed and stored in granules.

questions.q: A 35-year-old woman with diffuse hair loss notices her hair falls out in bunches while combing, 3 months after delivering a baby. Trichogram reveals >25% telogen hairs. The pathophysiology involves:
opts: Synchronised shift of follicles into telogen phase due to hormonal changes postpartum
Iron deficiency causing premature catagen entry
questions.exp: Telogen effluvium postpartum occurs due to synchronised shift of hair follicles from anagen to telogen phase, triggered by the fall in oestrogen levels after delivery. High oestrogen during pregnancy prolongs anagen; its withdrawal causes synchronous telogen entry. Shedding peaks at 3-4 months postpartum.

questions.q: A 50-year-old diabetic presents with a rapidly expanding, painful, necrotic wound on the lower leg with violaceous undermined edges, preceded by minor trauma. Cultures grow Pseudomonas aeruginosa. The diagnosis is:
questions.exp: Ecthyma gangrenosum is a cutaneous manifestation of Pseudomonas aeruginosa bacteraemia, classically in immunocompromised patients. It presents as haemorrhagic pustules evolving into gangrenous ulcers. Differs from pyoderma gangrenosum (pathergy, associated with IBD) and necrotising fasciitis (polymicrobial, deeper tissue).

questions.q: A 45-year-old woman presents with Raynaud phenomenon, sclerodactyly, telangiectasias, and heartburn. Anti-centromere antibody is positive. She is at increased risk of developing:
questions.exp: Anti-centromere antibodies are associated with limited cutaneous systemic sclerosis (lcSSc/CREST syndrome). The major visceral complication in lcSSc is pulmonary arterial hypertension (PAH). Renal crisis and severe ILD are more characteristic of diffuse cutaneous SSc with anti-Scl-70 (anti-topoisomerase I) antibodies.

questions.q: A 32-year-old man presents with shallow, painful oral ulcers along with crops of small vesicles on the genitalia, healing spontaneously in 10 days. He recalls 4 similar episodes in the past year. HSV serology is negative. Pathergy test is positive. The diagnosis is:
questions.exp: Behcet disease is characterised by recurrent oral aphthous ulcers, genital ulcers, uveitis, and skin lesions (pathergy positivity). Diagnosis is clinical (International Study Group criteria). It is more common along the 'Silk Road'. Colchicine and immunosuppressants are used for treatment.

questions.q: A 70-year-old man presents with a slowly enlarging, pearly, translucent papule with rolled edges and telangiectasias on the nose. The most important risk factor for this lesion and the first-line treatment are:
opts: Immunosuppression; surgical excision with Mohs micrographic surgery
Chronic sun exposure; surgical excision (standard or Mohs)
questions.exp: Basal cell carcinoma (BCC) is the most common skin cancer, primarily caused by chronic UV (sun) exposure. The nodular type presents as a pearly papule with rolled borders and telangiectasias. Standard surgical excision or Mohs micrographic surgery (for high-risk/facial sites) is first-line treatment.

questions.q: A 25-year-old with severe nodulocystic acne is started on isotretinoin. Which of the following monitoring parameters is most critical during therapy?
opts: Fasting lipid profile and liver function tests
questions.exp: Isotretinoin can cause hypertriglyceridaemia, hypercholesterolaemia, and elevated liver enzymes. Fasting lipid profile and LFTs must be monitored before starting and at 4-8 week intervals. It is also a potent teratogen requiring pregnancy prevention (iPLEDGE programme). CBC changes are rarely clinically significant.

questions.q: A biopsy from a hypopigmented patch in a leprosy patient shows granulomas composed of epithelioid cells surrounded by lymphocytes, with a Fite stain showing no AFB. The nerve is well-defined within the granuloma. This histopathology corresponds to:
questions.exp: Tuberculoid leprosy (TT) shows well-formed epithelioid granulomas with Langhans giant cells, surrounded by dense lymphocytic infiltrate. AFB are absent (paucibacillary). The granulomas invade and erode the epidermis and perineural sheath. Nerves are destroyed within the granuloma.

questions.q: A 30-year-old woman on hydroxychloroquine for lupus erythematosus needs ophthalmic monitoring. The recommended screening interval and the type of toxicity to monitor is:
opts: Annual after 5 years of use; retinal toxicity (bull's eye maculopathy)
questions.exp: Hydroxychloroquine causes retinal toxicity (bull's eye maculopathy) due to accumulation in the RPE. Current AAO guidelines recommend baseline exam then annual screening after 5 years of use (earlier if risk factors present). The critical test is 10-2 visual field and mfERG/SD-OCT.

questions.q: A 55-year-old woman presents with diffuse brownish hyperpigmentation in sun-exposed areas and a history of using a topical skin-lightening cream containing hydroquinone for over 3 years. The paradoxical hyperpigmentation from long-term hydroquinone use is called:
questions.exp: Exogenous ochronosis is a paradoxical hyperpigmentation caused by long-term use of high-concentration hydroquinone, more common in darker skin types (Fitzpatrick IV-VI). Clinically presents as blue-black or brown-grey hyperpigmentation in sun-exposed areas. Histology shows ochre-coloured banana-shaped fibres in the dermis.

questions.q: A 40-year-old man presents with 4-week history of painful, tender nodules on the shins with overlying erythema. He has associated fever, joint pain, and bilateral hilar lymphadenopathy on CXR. The most likely diagnosis and causative association is:
questions.exp: Lofgren syndrome is a triad of erythema nodosum + bilateral hilar lymphadenopathy + arthritis/arthralgia, representing an acute form of sarcoidosis with good prognosis. EN is a septal panniculitis (most common panniculitis). Treatment is NSAIDs for EN; sarcoidosis may require steroids.

questions.q: A 20-year-old develops flaccid blisters and erosions predominantly on mucous membranes with positive Nikolsky sign. DIF shows intercellular IgG deposits in a 'chicken-wire' pattern throughout the epidermis. Circulating antibodies target desmoglein 3 predominantly. This is:
questions.exp: Pemphigus vulgaris (PV) with predominantly anti-desmoglein 3 antibodies causes mucosal dominant disease (oral erosions). When both anti-dsg1 and anti-dsg3 are present, mucocutaneous involvement occurs. DIF shows intercellular IgG (tombstone pattern). Nikolsky sign is positive. Treated with systemic corticosteroids ± rituximab.

questions.q: A 24-year-old HIV-positive patient presents with multiple vascular papules and plaques on the lower extremities and oral mucosa. Biopsy shows spindle cell proliferation with slit-like vascular spaces and extravasated erythrocytes. HHV-8 DNA is detected by PCR. The diagnosis is:
questions.exp: Kaposi sarcoma (KS) in AIDS (epidemic KS) is caused by HHV-8 (KSHV). It presents as violaceous-to-brown vascular plaques/nodules on lower extremities and oral mucosa. Histology shows spindle cells, slit-like vascular channels, and erythrocyte extravasation. HAART is the cornerstone of treatment.

questions.q: A 48-year-old woman presents with intense pruritus without primary skin lesions. She has scleral icterus and pale stools. Pruritus is worse at night. Labs show elevated alkaline phosphatase and conjugated bilirubin. The likely mechanism of pruritus is:
opts: Increased histamine from mast cell activation
Accumulation of bile salts in skin activating nerve fibres
Elevated serum lysophosphatidic acid (LPA) activating sensory neurones
questions.exp: Cholestatic pruritus was historically attributed to bile salt deposition, but current evidence implicates elevated lysophosphatidic acid (LPA), an autotaxin product, as the primary pruritogen. LPA activates sensory nerve fibres. Rifampicin and obeticholic acid are treatment options. Bile salt sequestrants (cholestyramine) have modest efficacy.

questions.q: A 35-year-old man presents with scaly plaques on scalp, elbows, and knees. His nail examination reveals pitting, onycholysis, and subungual hyperkeratosis. The characteristic histopathological feature of the skin lesion is:
opts: Munro microabscesses and parakeratosis with absence of granular layer
questions.exp: Psoriasis histopathology shows regular acanthosis, parakeratosis with absent granular layer, Munro microabscesses (neutrophils in stratum corneum), Kogoj spongiform pustules (neutrophils in spinosum), and dilated tortuous capillaries in elongated dermal papillae.

questions.q: A 30-year-old presents with well-demarcated hypopigmented macules on the face, neck, and chest. Wood's lamp examination shows chalky white fluorescence. KOH examination of skin scrapings reveals the 'spaghetti and meatballs' pattern. The treatment of choice is:
opts: Oral terbinafine 250 mg daily for 4 weeks
Topical selenium sulphide or ketoconazole shampoo; oral itraconazole for extensive cases
questions.exp: Pityriasis versicolor is caused by Malassezia furfur (and related species). KOH shows short hyphae and clusters of round spores ('spaghetti and meatballs'). Topical antifungals (selenium sulphide, ketoconazole, zinc pyrithione) are first-line. Oral itraconazole 200 mg/day for 5 days or fluconazole is used for extensive disease.

questions.q: A neonate develops a localised area of skin loss at birth over the scalp vertex, with a sharply demarcated, clean, oval ulcer. No other lesions are present. The diagnosis is:
questions.exp: Aplasia cutis congenita (ACC) presents as congenital localised skin defect, most commonly on the scalp vertex. It appears as a well-demarcated ulcer or erosion at birth. Most cases are isolated (Group 1); associations with trisomy 13, Adams-Oliver syndrome exist. Small lesions heal with scarring; large defects may need grafting.

questions.q: A 55-year-old man with Type 2 DM presents with velvety, hyperpigmented plaques in the axillae and neck folds. Similar lesions are noted on the knuckles. Insulin resistance is confirmed. This skin sign is best explained by:
opts: IGF-1 and insulin receptor activation stimulating keratinocyte and fibroblast proliferation
Deposition of glycosylated proteins in the dermis
questions.exp: Acanthosis nigricans (AN) in insulin resistance/obesity is driven by hyperinsulinaemia: excess insulin binds IGF-1 receptors on keratinocytes and fibroblasts, stimulating their proliferation and causing the velvety epidermal thickening and hyperpigmentation. Malignancy-associated AN involves TGF-α.

questions.q: A 28-year-old man presents with painful genital ulcers that are soft and highly tender, with a 'ragged' undermined edge. Associated tender unilateral inguinal lymphadenopathy (bubo) is present. The causative organism and appropriate treatment are:
opts: Haemophilus ducreyi; azithromycin 1 g single dose or ceftriaxone 250 mg IM
Klebsiella granulomatis; doxycycline 100 mg BD for 21 days
questions.exp: Chancroid is caused by Haemophilus ducreyi. It presents as painful ('soft chancre'), tender genital ulcer with ragged undermined edges and tender inguinal bubo. Treatment options: azithromycin 1 g PO single dose, ceftriaxone 250 mg IM single dose, or ciprofloxacin 500 mg BD for 3 days.

questions.q: A 40-year-old woman presents with violaceous, flat-topped papules on the flexor surface of wrists and oral lacy white striations (Wickham striae). The pathological mechanism involves:
opts: Type I hypersensitivity mediated by IgE
CD8+ T cell-mediated apoptosis of basal keratinocytes
B cell autoantibody production against epidermal antigens
questions.exp: Lichen planus is characterised by the '6 P's' (pruritic, planar, polygonal, purple papules). Pathologically, it is a T cell-mediated lichenoid reaction: activated CD8+ cytotoxic T lymphocytes recognise basal keratinocyte antigens and induce apoptosis (colloid/civatte bodies). Band-like lymphocytic infiltrate at DEJ is hallmark histology.

questions.q: A 65-year-old woman presents with an enlarging irregular pigmented lesion on the sole. Dermoscopy shows a parallel ridge pattern. The diagnosis and its significance is:
opts: Acral lentiginous melanoma; most common melanoma subtype in Fitzpatrick V-VI skin, requires wide local excision
Seborrhoeic keratosis; benign, no treatment needed
questions.exp: Acral lentiginous melanoma (ALM) presents on palms, soles, and nail unit. On dermoscopy, the parallel ridge pattern (pigmentation along ridges of acral skin) is specific for melanoma. ALM is the most common melanoma subtype in Asian, African, and Hispanic populations. Treatment is wide local excision with sentinel node biopsy.
